title: Freya and the Wolf
premise: Paloma Thackeray flees her hedge-witch mistress into the Stillwater Valley, where magic cannot follow — the only place a dying stranger can safely press a blood-inked map into her hands. The map hides the true name of the Wolf, an ancient guardian the usurper King Aldric believes he slew, and Paloma discovers she is the Wolf's last living vessel, her lost childhood memories the key to waking it. Hunted by Aldric's inquisitor and betrayed by the loyal friend who sold her name to save his family, Paloma must choose between the truth that will reignite the war and the lie that would let the free cities sleep on. In the end she surrenders her memories willingly to wake the Wolf, defeats Aldric at the gates of the free cities, and wakes with no past at all — except a stranger who refuses to stop reminding her who she was.
about_author: Coral Fairweather is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval herbals before turning to fiction full-time. She writes fantasy about memory and belonging from a crooked cottage on the Welsh coast.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She slips away from her hedge-witch mistress Maren at dawn, crossing the boundary stones into the Stillwater Valley, where her magic gutters out like a wet wick. Relief wars with grief as she takes work at a waystation inn. Emotional beat: freedom that feels suspiciously like exile.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Door
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. During a storm, a wounded man in usurper's livery staggers into the inn and collapses at her feet. The innkeeper wants him out; Paloma, against every instinct to stay invisible, hides him in the cellar. Emotional beat: the first crack in her careful neutrality.

chapters.title: Blood and Ink
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The stranger, dying of a poisoned wound, presses a leather map into her hands and gasps a name — hers, or one she almost remembers. He dies as inquisitor Vane's riders reach the village. Emotional beat: terror and a terrible sense of recognition.

chapters.title: What Magic Cannot Follow
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She flees deeper into the valley, where the map's ink will not burn and Vane's trackers lose the scent. But the map whispers to her in dreams, showing a tower, a wolf, a door. Emotional beat: hunted, yet strangely chosen.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Daughter
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, with a flashback. She deciphers the map's maker's mark: her father's, the man Maren always refused to discuss. The valley's silence around magic, she realizes, was never accidental. Emotional beat: the ground of her identity shifts beneath her.

chapters.title: Tamsin of the Ford
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A free-city scout and old friend of the dead stranger catches up with Paloma at the river ford, sent to recover the map at any cost. She spares Paloma when the map won't leave her hands. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance, mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: The Road Out of Stillness
chapters.summary: Paloma and Tamsin's alternating POV. They leave the valley together; Paloma's suppressed magic floods back painfully, and the map begins to glow at her touch. Tamsin reveals Aldric burned the free cities' archives to erase the Wolf. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Inquisitor
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Cold and methodical, Vane interrogates the innkeeper, follows the map's residue, and reports to Aldric that the vessel lives. He carries a relic that can unmake memory. Emotional beat: menace as patience.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Archive
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. In a ruined library city, a blind archivist recognizes Paloma's face from pre-war portraits: she is the cartographer's daughter, hidden in the valley as a child. Emotional beat: grief for a childhood that was stolen, not lost.

chapters.title: The Wolf Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The map leads them to a sealed mountain gate; in her dreams, a great wolf speaks with her father's voice. She learns the guardian sleeps in a bloodline, not a body — hers. Emotional beat: awe and refusal.

chapters.title: A Bargain in Bramblewick
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Resupplying in a free city, Tamsin meets her brother, hostage to Aldric's court, who offers her family's safety if she delivers Paloma to Vane. Emotional beat: loyalty bending under love.

chapters.title: The Sold Name
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Vane ambushes them at a crossroads — guided by Tamsin's letter. Paloma escapes with the map but not her trust; Tamsin, weeping, confesses. Emotional beat: betrayal that is also a plea for forgiveness.

chapters.title: Alone with the Truth
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Wounded and alone, Paloma finally reads the map fully: waking the Wolf requires the vessel's willing surrender of every memory she has. She could instead burn the map and let the world forget. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh — loyalty vs. truth.

chapters.title: Vane's Offering
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Vane captures Paloma and, surprisingly, offers her a third path: give the map to Aldric, keep her memories, live rich and safe. For one long night she considers it. Emotional beat: temptation rendered honestly.

chapters.title: The Relic and the Knife
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She steals Vane's memory-unmaking relic during transfer to the capital and escapes with Tamsin, who has turned on her handlers to save her. They are bound now by shared guilt. Emotional beat: hard-won, unromanticized trust.

chapters.title: Aldric's Court
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. In the usurped capital, Aldric reveals he fears the Wolf not as a weapon but as a witness — the only being who remembers him as he truly was before the throne. Emotional beat: the villain given a wound.

chapters.title: The Gate of Names
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. At the mountain gate, Paloma speaks her father's true name and the door opens onto a hall of memory where the Wolf waits, wearing her own face. Emotional beat: confrontation with the self.

chapters.title: What I Would Keep
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The Wolf lets her choose what to keep: she keeps Tamsin's face, Maren's lullaby, the smell of the valley — and lets the rest go. Emotional beat: sacrifice as authorship, not loss.

chapters.title: The Wolf Wakes
chapters.summary: Paloma and Aldric's POV. Aldric's armies reach the free cities as the Wolf rises through Paloma's emptied body; Vane, seeing the relic fail, breaks. Aldric meets the guardian on the field and is unmade by remembered truth. Emotional beat: climax — war averted by witness, not slaughter.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Name
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The armies stand down; the free cities debate what to do with a guardian and a girl who no longer knows herself. Tamsin refuses to let Paloma be a monument. Emotional beat: tenderness after ruin.

chapters.title: The Stranger Who Remembers
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Memoryless but whole, Paloma returns to the valley with Tamsin, who tells her their story every night like a bedtime tale. The Wolf sleeps in the mountain, patient. Emotional beat: quiet, aching hope.

chapters.title: Freya and the Wolf
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. On the anniversary, Tamsin gives her a new name — Freya, the name her father whispered to the dying stranger — and the first memory returns unbidden: her father's hands on the map. She smiles, and begins again. Emotional beat: identity rebuilt as gift, not inheritance.
